policy.migration_rule: Do not migrate an installed or built-in plugin until a synthetic worker passes lifecycle, crash, timeout, cancellation, capability and cleanup gates.
policy.resource_attribution_rule: Per-plugin CPU and memory may only be reported for a dedicated worker process; in-process estimates are not accepted as attribution.

shared_worker_contract.host_api_rule: Worker capability calls must use explicit serializable proxy contracts and must re-enter PluginAccessContext in the host before permission checks and side effects.

profiles.current_boundary: Collectible AssemblyLoadContext inside the host process with direct ILongPlugin and IHostApi object calls.
profiles.ui_boundary: All current native assets expose host-owned WPF UI and cannot cross a process boundary as CLR objects.
profiles.target_model: Keep WPF presentation in the host; permit an opt-in headless command and lifecycle worker only after proxy contracts exist.
blockers: ILongPlugin receives the non-serializable IHostApi service graph directly.
IHasMainUI and WPF controls are returned as in-process CLR objects.
Optional lifecycle interfaces and events have no worker protocol contract.
Native dependencies and plugin-created threads require deterministic worker cleanup rules.

profiles.current_boundary: Roslyn executes the script in the host process and injects HostProvider through ScriptGlobals.
profiles.ui_boundary: The current script contract is headless, but delegates capture host-process objects and state.
profiles.target_model: Compile and execute in a dedicated worker after replacing ScriptGlobals.Host with a serializable capability proxy.
blockers: Start, Stop and language delegates have no remote invocation contract.
The current unload operation removes bookkeeping but cannot terminate script-created work.
There is no production script asset to provide migration compatibility evidence.

profiles.current_boundary: Web content uses the WebView2 process model while its WPF control, lifecycle adapter and host bridge dispatcher remain in the host process.
profiles.ui_boundary: Retain WebView2 ownership in the host workspace; do not introduce a second Long worker around browser content.
profiles.target_model: Harden the existing bounded JSON bridge and WebView2 process controls instead of duplicating UI isolation.
blockers: WebView2 WPF controls are host-owned presentation objects.
The host dispatcher maps bridge methods directly to IHostApi services.
Commands, widgets, navigation and focus depend on the current host presentation lifecycle.

profiles.current_boundary: The WebView2 UI and native background DLL share one in-host lifecycle adapter and direct IHostApi instance.
profiles.ui_boundary: Keep the WebView2 UI in the host; only the headless native background is a future worker candidate.
profiles.target_model: Split the native background into a worker while preserving one logical plugin lifecycle and a host-mediated open-request event.
blockers: OpenRequested is an in-process CLR event.
Web and background start-stop rollback is coordinated with direct object calls.
Clipboard monitoring and hotkey resources need crash-safe host cleanup and lease semantics.
